Use the guide Cookie policy Cookies are small files saved on your phone, tablet or computer when you visit a website. We use cookies to make the DfE Design manual work and collect information about how you use this website. Essential cookies Essential cookies keep your information secure while you use the DfE Design Manual. We do not need to ask permission to use them. Name Purpose Expires cookie-preferences Saves your cookie consent settings 1 year Analytics cookies (optional) With your permission, we use Google Analytics to collect data about how you use this service. This information helps us to improve our service. Google is not allowed to use or share our analytics data with anyone. Google Analytics stores anonymised information about: how you got to these sites the pages you visit and how long you spend on each page what you click on while you’re visiting these sites Name Purpose Expires _ga Helps us count how many people visit the DfE Design Manual by tracking if you’ve visited before 1 year CLID Used by Microsoft Clarity to help us understand DfE Design Manual usage 1 year MUID Used by Microsoft Clarity to help us understand DfE Design Manual usage 1 year Do you want to accept analytics cookies? Yes No Save cookie settings Components Components are reusable parts of a user interface. Using pre-built, core elements allows teams to build consistent services. In progress Component Summary Vertical navigation Let users navigate a series of pages with navigation aside the main content. Backlog Component Summary Charting Consistent and accessible charting in products. Interruption page Component for making users stop in a journey and take notice of some guidance. Progress bar A view which shows the steps or progress in a journey. If you have a component you want to see in the design system, follow the contribution guidelines. Design system DfE FrontendDfE Frontend extends GOV.UK Frontend and includes: styles components patterns When to use DfE FrontendUse DfE Frontend when designing and developing digital services for DfE. It ensures: a consistent user experience across DfE services alignment with the Digital Product Branding standard faster development by reusing ready-made components and styles DfE Frontend should be used by designers and developers working on public-facing services, internal applications, and digital tools that are part of the department’s digital ecosystem. Get startedTo start using DfE Frontend, follow the install DfE Frontend instructions. Contribute to DfE FrontendWhere you identify a pattern or component in a product that could be reused, consider contributing it to DfE Frontend. Doing this will also ensure you are working to meet Service Standard point 13, Use and contribute to open standards, common components and patterns. To contribute to DfE Frontend, follow the contribute to DfE Frontend instructions. Design Contribute to DfE FrontendContribute to the DfE Frontend design system by adding new components, fixing bugs, and improving the documentation. How to contributeThere are a number of ways you can contribute to the DfE Frontend design system: submit a pull request in the DfE Frontend GitHub repository join the patterns and components working group speak to DesignOps to discuss your contribution Patterns and components working groupThe patterns and components working group is a cross-discipline team of designers and developers that meets regularly to discuss and review new components and patterns for the design system. What we're working on Name Type Description Vertical nav Component Component for a styled vertical navigation for sections of a service. Contact the working group if you want to join or present something for review. Contribution guidelinesBefore you contribute to the DfE Frontend design system, you must check that the component or pattern you are adding or updating meets the following criteria: Download contribution criteria checklist (CSV - opens in Excel) UsefulYou can demonstrate that this component or pattern would be useful for other DfE teams or services. The need for the pattern or component has been validated through user research. Evidence could be screenshots or links to versions of it being used in different services. UniqueIt does not replicate something already in the GOV.UK or DfE Design Systems. UsersThere are other user groups completing similar tasks who would benefit from this component or pattern. Technical requirementsAll components must be: open source easily reusable without additional technical support (the guidance should be enough to implement) free from proprietary or closed-source dependencies free from dependencies which incur a licensing cost to use Check the backlogIf your idea is not on the DfE Frontend backlog and meets the criteria above, add an issue. If you cannot access the project or add an issue, contact the DesignOps team to discuss it. What to includeAt this stage, you just need to present your idea and evidence of the user needs. You can include screenshots or links to versions of the component or pattern in use, but avoid spending time working on a specific design or writing code. Contribution processThe contribution process follows these steps: Idea Present your idea and evidence of user needs to the Components Working Group Research and evidence Gather and validate user research to support the component or pattern Components Working Group review Review gate with the Components Working Group to proceed to design Design Create designs that meet the contribution guidelines Test Test designs with users to validate the approach Components Working Group review Review gate with the Components Working Group to proceed to build Build Develop the component or pattern code. Write and test all implementation guidance Publish all source code in a Public GitHub repository Accessibility audit Ensure the component or pattern meets accessibility standards. You must have the component audited before it is used by end users. Test Test the implementation with users Approval review Present to the patterns and components working group for approval Publish Release the component or pattern to the design system Maintain Continue to maintain and improve the component or pattern based on feedback Design system Install DfE Frontend Step-by-step guide for installing the DfE Frontend package into your product This guide is currently written for people wanting to use DfE Frontend in a prototype and using VS Code. If you are looking to use it in .NET apps and unsure how to proceed, contact DesignOps. Prerequisites You will need to have the following installed: Node.js VS Code You will also need to have a prototype set up in VS Code. Follow the instructions on the GOV.UK service manual to get a new prototype up and running. Install the package 1. Install Copy code Run this command in your terminal in VS Code to install the DfE Frontend package. npm install dfe-frontend CSS, JavaScript, and logo files 2. application.scss Copy code Add this to the top of your application.scss file to include the DfE Frontend CSS file, after importing GOV Frontend classes. @import 'node_modules/dfe-frontend/packages/dfefrontend'; JavaScript 3. layout file Copy code Add this to the bottom of your layout file to include the DfE Frontend JavaScript file. {% block scripts %} {{ super() }} <script src="/assets/js/dfefrontend.min.js"></script> {% endblock %} Copy the logo files 4. Copy image assets Copy these files to your project's assets/images folder. You may need to create this folder if it does not exist. /node_modules/dfe-frontend/packages/assets/dfe-logo.png /node_modules/dfe-frontend/packages/assets/dfe-logo-alt.png Changing the page width 5. Set page width to 1200px Copy code This will set the page width to 1200px. You can adjust this to suit your needs and overrides the GOV.UK smaller 960px width. .govuk-width-container { @include govuk-width-container; } Typography 6. Install DfE typography If your site is on education.gov, you must use the Inter typeface and install DfE typography. You can skip this step if your site is not on education.gov. Run your app 7. Run your app Copy code In your terminal in VS Code, run this command. It will build and start the app, and you can view it in your browser. npm run dev Back to design system Professions Figma Training and guidance for using Figma in DfE services. How to use the DWP Design System
externalText: Designing for everyone This is the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) design system. It includes standard design elements and best practice for DWP digital services. Use the DWP Design System alongside the GOV.UK Design System. Components Patterns Templates Guidance Open questions File upload How can we help users upload files to a service? Filters Do we need a standard way for users to filter information? We need teams to test and tell us what they find Design for... Evidence What does the user need to know before they can decide? History What actions, decisions, or events have occurred? Identity Components and patterns relevant in an identity context See all Get started What are design systems? Types of design system and what to expect from DWP guidance and patterns How to use the DWP Design System A guide to using patterns and components in your project Install DWP Frontend Use npm and DWP Frontend to add components to your service Propose a new component, pattern or template Have an idea for a repeatable pattern that could be part of the Design System? Let us know. Horizontal navigation A horizontal container for secondary navigation links within a service Contents The horizontal navigation component is a list of secondary navigation links within a service. It is included in DWP Frontend. Desktop view of Horizontal navigation - default Tablet view of Horizontal navigation - default Mobile view of Horizontal navigation - default Open in new tab When to use this componentUse this component when users need to move between related pages within a service. The horizontal navigation component is for use in internal services. It is intended as secondary navigation: for primary navigation you should use the internal service header with the navigation option. It is one of two options for secondary navigation within a service: the other is side navigation. When to consider something elseYou should not use horizontal navigation as the main navigation in a service. Use the internal service header with the navigation option instead. You should not use this component in public-facing services. If you need secondary navigation consider the GOV.UK Service navigation component instead. Do not use this component for internal links between sections of the same page. If you need to organise large amounts of content on a single page consider the GOV.UK Tabs component instead. Design goals and metricsThere are various ways of implementing secondary navigation across DWP services. The design goal is to establish a standard. Get support Need help implementing this in a prototype or production build? Get support from the Design System team. Give feedback We depend on insights from real projects to update and improve the design system. If you use something we made, tell us how it went. Could we improve this page? Send questions, comments or suggestions to the DWP Design System team. Last updated: 1 October 2024

externalText: Design your service using GOV.UK styles, components and patterns Use this design system to make government services consistent with GOV.UK. Learn from the research and experience of other service teams and avoid repeating work that’s already been done. Get started What’s new 27 August 2026: We’ve released GOV.UK Frontend v6.5.0 This release adds the Feedback component to help you gather feedback from your users and the Language navigation component to let your users switch between languages your service offers. Both these components have been released as ‘Trial’ components, using our new component lifecycle statuses. See each component’s guidance page to learn how you can help us move them to ‘Stable’ status. Read the release notes for v6.5.0 on GitHub to see what’s changed or see our latest updates on the What’s new page. Get updates on the Design System Interested in changes to the Design System, or our upcoming events and workshops? Sign up with your email Styles Make government services look like GOV.UK with guides for applying layout, typography, colour and images. Browse our styles Components Save time with reusable, accessible components for forms, navigation, panels, tables and more. Browse our components Patterns Help users complete common tasks like entering names and addresses, filling in forms and creating accounts. Browse our patterns Update your service to use the refreshed GOV.UK brand In June 2025, GOV.UK started to refresh the brand across its products and services. To support this, we’ve released several versions of GOV.UK Frontend to help teams update their services. Find out how to update your service to use the refreshed brand. Principles we follow The GOV.UK Design System helps teams that work on government services follow the Government Design Principles and GOV.UK Service Manual. This website also follows the GOV.UK style guide and GOV.UK content and publishing guidance. Our accessibility strategy outlines our principles and work to improve accessibility within the GOV.UK Design System. Community The GOV.UK Design System is for everyone that works on government services, with a strong community sitting behind it. It brings together the latest research, design and development from across government to make sure it’s representative and relevant for its users. You can help improve the Design System by joining our discussions, events and co-design collaborations. Also see upcoming components and patterns we’re working on and how you can help. Support The GOV.UK Design System is maintained by a team at the Government Digital Service. If you’ve got a question, idea or suggestion, you can contact the team. See blog posts, video talks, and podcasts about the GOV.UK Design System and Prototype Kit. Roadmap See what the Design System team at GDS is planning to work on over the next 12 months in the GOV.UK Design System Roadmap.

profession: Interaction designer, Content designer, Service designer
externalTitle: HMRC patterns for services - Design resources for HMRC — GOV.UK
externalText: These are patterns designed specifically for the needs of HMRC users and patterns that are not yet in the GOV.UK Design System. Check the GOV.UK Design System to see if the component or pattern you need is already being used across government. If you cannot find what you need in the GOV.UK Design System or the HMRC design patterns, you can: see if it is being worked on by other teams across government and add your findings see if it is being worked on by HMRC and add your findings propose a new pattern All patterns must meet the contribution criteria. Using code snippets in prototypes Each pattern includes coded examples. You will need to install HMRC Frontend to use patterns with specific HMRC code not yet supported by the GOV.UK Prototype Kit. You must use version 7 or later of the GOV.UK Prototype Kit for these to work. Find out how to set up the Prototype Kit. Get help If you have a question, idea or suggestion you can: email the design resources team at design.resources-g@digital.hmrc.gov.uk get in touch through Slack (opens in app if you have it) Design your service Use these design resources to make your service and guidance consistent with HMRC and GOV.UK. Learn from the experience of other teams to avoid repeating work and share your knowledge by suggesting new content. Start now What’s new 28 July 2026: Goods Movement Reference published 9 July 2026: HMRC email updates, videos and webinars updated (changes) 7 July 2026: Pay for a tax, duty, levy or grant updated (changes) 23 June 2026: Technical guidance archived 9 June 2026: Factsheets updated (changes) Check all updates to HMRC design resources Styles, components and patterns HMRC patterns for services Design HMRC services with reusable, accessible patterns based on the research and experience of other service teams. HMRC patterns for GOV.UK Design specialist HMRC content on GOV.UK using these pre-agreed content patterns. HMRC style guide Use the HMRC style guide for HMRC-specific terms, styles and conventions. Principles we follow HMRC design resources supplement GOV.UK Design System. It follows the GOV.UK Government Design Principles, Service Standard and content design guidance. HMRC also follows the GOV.UK accessibility strategy to improve the accessibility of our services. Contribute If you have a question, idea or suggestion: get in touch to propose new patterns or share your knowledge: design.resources-g@digital.hmrc.gov.uk get in touch through Slack (opens in app if you have it)
